summary: Canary routing table flap causes tenant-specific 5xx wave; dedicated GPUs hit nvmlDeviceReset and runtime crashloop
description: Issue summary: Customer Acme Retail observed a sharp increase in 5xx responses beginning 2026-03-13 02:12 UTC for requests routed to their dedicated pool. API Gateway returned predominantly 502/503 for short-lived requests and 504 for long streaming sessions. Impact: ~35% error rate for the tenant over a 25-minute window, customer reports production failures for search/summary flows. Timeline: Canary routing table update (route-manager rollout) at 02:08 UTC introduced a new model variant with route weights; by 02:12 traffic became unevenly distributed and a subset of dedicated GPUs experienced repeated nvmlDeviceReset events. Multiple runtime workers entered crashloop and downstream API Gateway started returning 502s as upstream connections closed. This ticket tracks the investigation, mitigations applied, and follow-ups.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Trigger canary deployment in route-manager that shifts 30% weight to new model-variant X for tenant Acme
2) Send steady traffic profile simulating search-heavy workload (long prompts, high token output) from a single tenant identity
3) Observe routing table; if route assignment pins many sessions to a small set of worker pods, watch for increased GPU memory fragmentation and watchdog resets
4) API Gateway logs will show increased upstream 502s/503s and connection resets as runtimes restart
logs_and_metrics: api-gateway 502 spike: 02:12:15 -> 02:37:40 UTC, error-rate for tenant: peak 38%
runtime logs (worker-57): 'nvmlDeviceReset(): device 0: GPU watchdog triggered' repeated every ~45s, followed by process exit code 137
dmesg excerpt on runtime node: 'NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:af:00): 31, GPU has fallen off the bus'
autoscaler metrics: dedicated-pool-utilization jumped from 54% -> 97% within 3m; no new nodes provisioned due to capacity floor policy
apigw trace id example: trace=rz-8a1f-02, upstream-addr=10.2.17.89:8080, upstream-status=500, upstream-error='connection reset by peer'
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: canary weight distribution caused traffic concentration on a small shard of worker pods -> memory pressure and kvcache thrash
Confirmed repeated nvmlDeviceReset on a consistent subset of GPU hosts (host-rt-57, host-rt-58) correlating with the crashloop times

Kernel fallback not observed; runtime was on production kernel and used CUDA 12.1 + NVIDIA driver 525.85.05 — driver shows known edge-case with fragmentation when multiple model variants hot-swap large KV caches
Autoscaler did not scale because policy prevented scale-up during canary (safety limit). This allowed sustained high utilization -> device watchdogs fired

API Gateway returned 502/503 as it detected unhealthy upstream sockets and started short-circuiting to failover; failover capacity did not absorb tenant traffic due to route weights pinned at canary tier
comments: 2026-03-13 02:40 UTC — Lena Torres (Support): Notified customer, opened incident bridge, requested CS to throttle non-critical jobs. Asked infra to revert canary if unstable.

2026-03-13 02:45 UTC — Marcus Chen (SRE): Scaled a small emergency hotpool (2 nodes) in us-west-2 and applied soft-route fallback to shift canary traffic off the failing hosts; observed error-rate drop to ~7% within 6m

2026-03-13 03:05 UTC — Priya Nair (Runtime Eng): Collected core dumps and nvml logs from host-rt-57/58. Initial binary-level inspection points to fragmentation causing nvml resets when large KV caches are swapped in close succession.
2026-03-13 03:22 UTC — Customer (Acme Ops): Confirmed our ingestion queue is back to normal; asked for RCA and whether pinning model version prevents reoccurrence.
2026-03-13 05:10 UTC — Marcus Chen (SRE): Temporarily disabled canary weighting for Acme tenant and set route fallback to route-group 'stable' until further testing completed. Monitoring continues.
temporary_workaround: 1) Reverted canary routing weights for Acme to 0% for the new variant (route-manager rollback at 02:47 UTC)
2) Emergency hotpool of 2 dedicated GPU nodes provisioned and added to tenant pool to absorb overload
3) Applied a soft rate-limit on long streaming sessions for the tenant for 30 minutes to reduce tail pressure
root_cause_hypothesis: A combination of canary routing table weight skew + autoscaler safety limits concentrated traffic on a small number of dedicated GPU hosts while a new model-variant was hot-swapped into those workers. Repeated large KV cache allocations and deallocations produced GPU memory fragmentation that triggered nvmlDeviceReset watchdogs, causing runtime processes to crash and upstream 5xx waves.
resolution: In progress — mitigations applied (canary rollback and hotpool scale). Runtime engineering is reproducing locally with controlled KV eviction tests. Planned fix options: 1) change route-manager canary rollout to respect per-pool capacity thresholds; 2) adjust autoscaler policy to allow quick emergency scale for dedicated pools during canary; 3) introduce kvcache pre-warm heuristics and staged hot-swap to avoid large contiguous allocations. Expected ETA for patching rollout: 2026-03-18 pending verification.
next_steps: - Runtime Eng to produce reproducible test-case for nvml reset with current driver (assigned Priya)
- Infra to add capacity-aware canary guard in route-manager (PR referenced above) and add a temporary guardrail for dedicated pools by 2026-03-16
- Postmortem to be drafted in Confluence with timeline and follow-ups once root cause is confirmed
- CS to follow up with customer by 2026-03-14 12:00 PDT with update and mitigation summary
